claim: Cardiac β-myosin variants cause hypertrophic (HCM) or dilated (DCM) cardiomyopathy by disrupting sarcomere contraction and relaxation.
source: Cardiac β-myosin variants cause hypertrophic (HCM) or dilated (DCM) cardiomyopathy by disrupting sarcomere contraction and relaxation.
evidence: This is a foundational statement in the abstract supported by established scientific knowledge about cardiomyopathy pathogenesis.

claim: The locations of variants on isolated myosin head structures predict contractility effects but not the prominent relaxation and energetic deficits that characterize HCM.
source: The locations of variants on isolated myosin head structures predict contractility effects but not the prominent relaxation and energetic deficits that characterize HCM.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in current understanding based on prior research, setting up the rationale for the study.

claim: During relaxation, pairs of myosins form interacting-heads motif (IHM) structures that with other sarcomere proteins establish an energy-saving, super-relaxed (SRX) state.
source: During relaxation, pairs of myosins form interacting-heads motif (IHM) structures that with other sarcomere proteins establish an energy-saving, super-relaxed (SRX) state.
evidence: This describes established structural biology knowledge about myosin organization during relaxation.

claim: A human β-cardiac myosin IHM quasi-atomic model (PDB 5TBY) was created and used to define interaction sites between adjacent myosin heads and associated protein partners.
source: Using a human β-cardiac myosin IHM quasi-atomic model, we defined interactions sites between adjacent myosin heads and associated protein partners
evidence: This describes a methodological approach and structural model developed in this study.

claim: Rare variants from 6112 HCM and 1315 DCM patients and 33,370 ExAC controls were analyzed.
source: we defined interactions sites between adjacent myosin heads and associated protein partners, and then analyzed rare variants from 6112 HCM and 1315 DCM patients and 33,370 ExAC controls.
evidence: This describes the patient cohort and control population used in the study.

claim: 72% of HCM variants changed electrostatic charges.
source: HCM variants, 72% that changed electrostatic charges
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the analysis of HCM variants.

claim: HCM variants disproportionately altered IHM interaction residues (expected 23%; HCM 54%, p=2.6×10−19; DCM 26%, p=0.66; controls 20%, p=0.23).
source: HCM variants, 72% that changed electrostatic charges, disproportionately altered IHM interaction residues (expected 23%; HCM 54%, p=2.6×10−19; DCM 26%, p=0.66; controls 20%, p=0.23).
evidence: This presents statistical analysis showing enrichment of HCM variants in IHM interaction sites.

claim: HCM variant locations predict impaired IHM formation and stability, and attenuation of the SRX state.
source: HCM variant locations predict impaired IHM formation and stability, and attenuation of the SRX state
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the structural analysis of variant locations.

claim: Impaired IHM formation and stability accounts for altered contractility, reduced diastolic relaxation, and increased energy consumption that fully characterizes HCM pathogenesis.
source: accounting for altered contractility, reduced diastolic relaxation, and increased energy consumption, that fully characterizes HCM pathogenesis.
evidence: This is the main conclusion linking structural findings to clinical phenotypes.

claim: Sarcomeres are composed of inter-digitating thick filaments that contain myosin and thin filaments that contain actin.
source: Sarcomeres are composed of inter-digitating thick filaments that contain myosin, comprising a globular head (subfragment 1; S1) and α-helical tail, and thin filaments that contain actin.
evidence: This is established knowledge about sarcomere structure.

claim: Interactions between myosin and actin generate the contractile force underpinning sarcomere contraction.
source: Interactions between myosin and actin generate the contractile force underpinning sarcomere contraction.
evidence: This is fundamental knowledge about muscle contraction mechanisms.

claim: Myosin heads comprise a motor domain (MD) that hydrolyses ATP, a regulatory domain (RD) that includes the essential (ELC) and regulatory (RLC) light chains, and a proximal S2 subfragment.
source: Myosin heads comprise a motor domain (MD) that hydrolyses ATP, a regulatory domain (RD) that includes the essential (ELC) and regulatory (RLC) light chains, and a proximal S2 subfragment.
evidence: This describes the structural organization of myosin based on established knowledge.

claim: Myosin tails are packed in antiparallel formation and shape the thick filament's backbone, from which myosin heads protrude every 14.3 nm as crowns formed by three pairs of heads.
source: Myosin tails are packed in antiparallel formation and shape the thick filament's backbone, from which myosin heads protrudes every 14.3 nm as crowns formed by three pairs of heads.
evidence: This describes the structural organization of thick filaments based on established knowledge.

claim: In some crowns the S2 fragment interacts with myosin binding protein-C (MyBP-C).
source: In some crowns (Zoghbi et al., 2008) the S2 fragment interacts with myosin binding protein-C (MyBP-C), another thick filament protein that modulates sarcomere activity.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Contraction occurs through conformational changes in the myosin MD that accompany ATP hydrolysis, increasing affinity for actin in the thin filament, and resulting in a powerstroke that transfers force by rotation of the myosin lever domain around the converter domain.
source: Contraction occurs through conformational changes in the myosin MD that accompany ATP hydrolysis, increasing affinity for actin in the thin filament, and resulting in a powerstroke that transfers force by rotation of the myosin lever domain around the converter domain.
evidence: This describes the established mechanism of muscle contraction.

claim: After contraction, myosin heads rebind ATP, detach from actin, and assume a relaxed pre-powerstroke state.
source: After contraction, myosin heads rebind ATP, detach from actin, and assume a relaxed pre-powerstroke state (Llinas et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes the relaxation phase of the contractile cycle, supported by citation.

claim: Consecutive IHMs interact along helices that protrude from the thick filament backbone and limit potential interactions between myosin heads and actin.
source: Consecutive IHMs interact along helices that protrude from the thick filament backbone and limit potential interactions between myosin heads and actin (Alamo et al., 2008; Jung et al., 2008).
evidence: This describes the organization of IHMs in the thick filament, supported by citations.

claim: The IHM forms only in relaxed muscle and is a highly conserved structure throughout the evolution of myosins among different species, in different muscle types (smooth, skeletal, and cardiac), and non-muscle myosins.
source: The IHM forms only in relaxed muscle and is a highly conserved structure throughout the evolution of myosins among different species, in different muscle types (smooth, skeletal, and cardiac), and non-muscle myosins (Alamo et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes the conservation and specificity of the IHM structure, supported by citation.

claim: The IHM appears to form through key interactions involving the actin-binding region of one myosin head (denoted as 'blocked') and the converter region of the partner 'free' head.
source: The IHM appears to form through key interactions (Figure 1A) involving the actin-binding region of one myosin head (denoted as 'blocked') and the converter region of the partner 'free' head (Woodhead et al., 2005; Alamo et al., 2008; Jung et al., 2008).
evidence: This describes the molecular basis of IHM formation, supported by citations and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: IHM priming occurs when the blocked head assumes a pre-powerstroke state and docks onto its own S2 by intra-molecular interactions.
source: IHM priming occurs when the blocked head assumes a pre-powerstroke state (Llinas et al., 2015) and docks onto its own S2 by intra-molecular interactions.
evidence: This describes a specific step in IHM formation, supported by citation.

claim: IHM anchoring occurs by inter-molecular interactions between the docked, blocked head and the neighboring myosin's tail, and intra-molecular interactions with its ELC.
source: IHM anchoring occurs by inter-molecular interactions between the docked, blocked head and the neighboring myosin's tail, and intra-molecular interactions with its ELC.
evidence: This describes another step in IHM formation based on structural analysis.

claim: IHM stabilization occurs by intra-molecular interactions between the free myosin head and the anchored blocked head.
source: IHM stabilization occurs by intra-molecular interactions between the free myosin head and the anchored blocked head (Alamo et al., 2008; Brito et al., 2011; Alamo et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes the stabilization step in IHM formation, supported by citations.

claim: IHM scaffolding interactions between myosin heads and both ELCs and RLCs further support its three-dimensional shape.
source: IHM scaffolding interactions between myosin heads and both ELCs and RLCs further support its three-dimensional shape.
evidence: This describes additional structural support for the IHM.

claim: The dynamic structure of the IHM enables properties that are not observed in isolated S1 myosin fragments: reduced ATPase activity in blocked heads and intermittently in the free head.
source: The dynamic structure of the IHM (Brito et al., 2011) enables properties that are not observed in isolated S1 myosin fragments (Figure 1A): (i) reduced ATPase activity in blocked heads and intermittently in the free head
evidence: This describes functional properties of the IHM, supported by citation and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: The IHM enables mobility of the free head, that sways forth and back by breaking and restoring stabilizing IHM interactions.
source: (ii) mobility of the free head, that sways forth and back by breaking and restoring stabilizing IHM interactions (Alamo et al., 2008; Brito et al., 2011; Sulbarán et al., 2013; Espinoza-Fonseca et al., 2015; Alamo et al., 2015; Yamaguchi et al., 2016; Alamo et al., 2016)
evidence: This describes the dynamic behavior of the free head in the IHM, supported by multiple citations.

claim: The IHM enables release of extra free heads upon activation and blocked heads for force potentiation.
source: (iii) release of extra free heads upon activation and blocked heads for force potentiation (Brito et al., 2011).
evidence: This describes the functional consequence of IHM dynamics during activation, supported by citation.

claim: Negatively stained smooth muscle myosins show that free heads are flexible, detaching from their partner blocked heads and adopting different motor domain orientations.
source: Consistent with these properties, negatively stained smooth muscle myosins show that free heads are flexible, detaching from their partner blocked heads and adopting different motor domain orientations (Burgess et al., 2007)
evidence: This is an observation from electron microscopy studies, supported by citation.

claim: Swaying free heads support the sliding of F-actin filaments along relaxed thick filaments.
source: that swaying free heads support the sliding of F-actin filaments along relaxed thick filaments (Brito et al., 2011)
evidence: This describes a functional property of swaying free heads, supported by citation.

claim: Thick filaments respond to calcium activation producing force immediately.
source: and that thick filament respond to calcium activation producing force immediately (Linari et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes the rapid response of thick filaments to activation, supported by citation.

claim: The blocked myosin head has a pre-powerstroke state while docked onto its S2, so ATPase activity is sterically inhibited, and the actin-binding interface is positioned on the converter domain of the free head, so that it cannot bind actin.
source: The blocked myosin head has a pre-powerstroke state (Xu et al., 2003; Zoghbi et al., 2004; Llinas et al., 2015) while docked onto its S2, so ATPase activity is sterically inhibited, and the actin-binding interface is positioned on the converter domain of the free head, so that it cannot bind actin.
evidence: This describes the structural and functional state of the blocked head, supported by citations.

claim: The asymmetric conformations of myosins could impact RLC phosphorylation, which modulates the rate and extent of force development in cardiac muscle.
source: In addition, the asymmetric conformations of myosins could also impact RLC phosphorylation, which modulates the rate and extent of force development in cardiac muscle (Toepfer et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential functional consequences, supported by citation.

claim: The RLC associated with the free head is more accessible to protein kinase C phosphorylation, which promotes swaying.
source: The RLC associated with the free head is more accessible to protein kinase C phosphorylation (Alamo et al., 2008), which promotes swaying (Brito et al., 2011) and potential actin interactions.
evidence: This describes differential accessibility of RLC for phosphorylation, supported by citations.

claim: When the free myosin head docks onto the blocked head, its ATPase is also inhibited through stabilization of converter domain movements that are needed to achieve strong actin binding.
source: When the free myosin head docks onto the blocked head, its ATPase is also inhibited through stabilization of converter domain movements that are needed to achieve strong actin binding (Wendt et al., 2001).
evidence: This describes the mechanism of ATPase inhibition in the SRX state, supported by citation.

claim: The dual enzymatic inhibition of SRX is reflected by a low ATP turnover rate, detected by quantitative epi-fluorescence in skeletal and cardiac relaxed muscle fibers.
source: The dual enzymatic inhibition of SRX is reflected by a low ATP turnover rate, detected by quantitative epi-fluorescence in skeletal (Stewart et al., 2010; Naber et al., 2011; McNamara et al., 2016) and cardiac (Hooijman et al., 2011) relaxed muscle fibers
evidence: This describes experimental evidence for the SRX state, supported by citations.

claim: The SRX state is proposed as an energy saving mechanism.
source: and is proposed as an energy saving mechanism (Cooke, 2011).
evidence: This is a proposed functional role for the SRX state, supported by citation.

claim: Muscle relaxation can be characterized by two myosin head IHM conformations and ATPase activities: the DRX state with swaying free myosin heads and ATPase rate comparable to that observed in single myosin molecules, and the SRX state with a highly inhibited (five-fold lower) ATPase rate.
source: Muscle relaxation can therefore be characterized by two myosin head IHM conformations and ATPase activities (Figure 1A): the DRX state with swaying free myosin heads and ATPase rate comparable to that observed in single myosin molecules, and the SRX state with a highly inhibited (five-fold lower) ATPase rate (Stewart et al., 2010; Naber et al., 2011; McNamara et al., 2016; Hooijman et al., 2011).
evidence: This summarizes the two relaxation states and their properties, supported by citations and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: Hypertrophic (HCM) and dilated (DCM) cardiomyopathies are heart muscle diseases caused by variants in genes encoding sarcomere proteins.
source: Hypertrophic (HCM) and dilated (DCM) cardiomyopathies are heart muscle diseases caused by variants in genes encoding sarcomere proteins (Geisterfer-Lowrance et al., 1990; Seidman and Seidman, 1991; Konno et al., 2010)
evidence: This is established knowledge about the genetic basis of cardiomyopathies, supported by citations.

claim: MYH7 (encoding cardiac β-myosin heavy chain) and MYPBC3 (encoding MyBP-C) are the most common genes causing cardiomyopathy.
source: most commonly MYH7 (encoding cardiac β-myosin heavy chain; MHC) and MYPBC3 (encoding MyBP-C) and rarely in MYL2 and MYL3 that encode the ELC and RLC, respectively.
evidence: This describes the relative frequency of variants in different sarcomere genes.

claim: Distinct variants in sarcomere genes also cause DCM, albeit less frequently.
source: Distinct variants in sarcomere genes also cause DCM, albeit less frequently.
evidence: This describes the genetic basis of DCM.

claim: Variant location is not highly predictive of whether it will trigger HCM or DCM.
source: Variant location is not highly predictive of whether it will trigger HCM or DCM (Colegrave and Peckham, 2014).
evidence: This describes a limitation in predicting disease phenotype from variant location, supported by citation.

claim: HCM hearts exhibit hyperdynamic contraction, impaired relaxation, and increased energy demands.
source: HCM hearts exhibit hyperdynamic contraction, impaired relaxation, and increased energy demands (Ashrafian et al., 2011).
evidence: This describes the clinical phenotype of HCM, supported by citation.

claim: Impaired relaxation (clinically denoted as diastolic dysfunction) is a major cause of HCM symptoms and arrhythmias.
source: Impaired relaxation (clinically denoted as diastolic dysfunction) is a major cause of HCM symptoms and arrhythmias.
evidence: This describes the clinical significance of diastolic dysfunction in HCM.

claim: Increased energy demands in HCM hearts are thought to contribute to cardiomyocyte death and progression to heart failure.
source: Increased energy demands in HCM hearts are thought to contribute to cardiomyocyte death and progression to heart failure.
evidence: This describes a proposed mechanism for HCM progression.

claim: HCM MYH7 variants increase myofibrillar Ca2+-sensitivity and sarcomere power, explaining hyperdynamic contraction.
source: Previous studies demonstrate that HCM MYH7 variants increase myofibrillar Ca2+-sensitivity and sarcomere power, therein explaining hyperdynamic contraction (Seidman and Seidman, 2001; Tyska et al., 2000; Moore et al., 2012; Spudich, 2014; Marston, 2011; Harris et al., 2011; Ashrafian et al., 2011; Spudich et al., 2016)
evidence: This summarizes prior research on HCM variant effects, supported by multiple citations.

claim: The mechanisms accounting for diminished relaxation and excessive energy requirements in HCM remain poorly understood.
source: but the mechanisms accounting for diminished relaxation and excessive energy requirements remain poorly understood.
evidence: This identifies a gap in current understanding that the study aims to address.

claim: DCM MYH7 variants decrease Ca2+-sensitivity and reduce motor domain functions, accounting for diminished contractile performance.
source: By contrast, DCM MYH7 variants decrease Ca2+-sensitivity and reduce motor domain functions (Debold et al., 2007; Moore et al., 2012; Spudich, 2014; Marston, 2011; Spudich et al., 2016), therein accounting for diminished contractile performance, the prototypic feature of DCM.
evidence: This summarizes prior research on DCM variant effects, supported by citations.

claim: Unlike HCM, diastolic dysfunction is uncommon early in the clinical course of DCM but emerges with myocardial remodeling.
source: Unlike HCM, diastolic dysfunction is uncommon early in the clinical course of DCM (Lakdawala et al., 2012) but emerges with myocardial remodeling.
evidence: This describes the clinical course of DCM, supported by citation.

claim: Disease-associated MYH7 variants cause single amino acid substitutions.
source: Disease-associated MYH7 variants cause single amino acid (aa) substitutions
evidence: This describes the nature of pathogenic variants.

claim: The locations of MYH7 variant substitutions inform physiologically important domains in myosin.
source: and as such the locations of these substitutions inform physiologically important domains in myosin.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the relationship between variant location and function.

claim: The impact of MYH7 variants on MD properties have been studied in the context of a variety of vertebrate molecular myosin structures.
source: Because myosin sequences are highly conserved across species, the impact of MYH7 variants on MD properties have been studied in the context of a variety of vertebrate molecular myosin structures.
evidence: This describes the approach used in prior studies.

claim: Early analyses employing chicken skeletal S1 myosin demonstrated that HCM variants perturbed MD residues involved in nucleotide-binding, actin-binding, or the relay, converter, and lever.
source: Early analyses, employing the chicken skeletal S1 myosin (Rayment et al., 1995, 1993), demonstrated that HCM variants perturbed MD residues involved in nucleotide-binding, actin-binding, or the relay, converter, and lever.
evidence: This summarizes findings from early structural studies, supported by citations.

claim: Additional HCM variants were located onto the myosin mesa, a newly characterized flat broad structural feature that is proposed to bind MyBP-C.
source: More recently additional HCM variants were located onto the myosin mesa (Homburger et al., 2016), a newly characterized flat broad (>20 nm2) structural feature that is proposed to bind MyBP-C (Spudich, 2015; Spudich et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes more recent findings about variant locations, supported by citations.

claim: The mesa is prominent in the pre-stroke S1 contractile state, but substantially reduced following the powerstroke.
source: The mesa is prominent in the pre-stroke S1 contractile state, but substantially reduced following the powerstroke (Homburger et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes the dynamic nature of the mesa structure, supported by citation.

claim: The tarantula striated IHM quasi-atomic model PDB 3DTP defines interactions between adjacent myosin heads and possible interactions with IHM-associated protein partners and the backbone.
source: The tarantula striated IHM quasi-atomic model PDB 3DTP (Alamo et al., 2008) complements these structures by defining interactions between adjacent myosin heads and possible interactions with IHM-associated protein partners and the backbone.
evidence: This describes a prior structural model used for analysis, supported by citation.

claim: Analyses of a few selected HCM variants hint that these may impact residues involved in IHM intra- and intermolecular interactions.
source: Harnessing this model with other structures (human S2 crystal PDB 2FXM model [Blankenfeldt et al., 2006] and chicken smooth muscle myosin PDB 1I84 model [Liu et al., 2003]), the analyses of a few selected HCM variants (Blankenfeldt et al., 2006; Alamo et al., 2008; Moore et al., 2012) hint that these may impact residues involved in IHM intra- and intermolecular interactions.
evidence: This describes prior limited analyses of HCM variants in the context of IHM, supported by citations.

claim: The study assessed the structural pathogenesis of HCM and DCM by comprehensive analyses of the largest series of genotyped cardiomyopathy cases, comprising 7427 individuals with clinical-grade sequencing.
source: Here we assessed the structural pathogenesis of HCM and DCM by comprehensive analyses of the largest series of genotyped cardiomyopathy cases, comprising 7427 individuals with clinical-grade sequencing (Walsh et al., 2017).
evidence: This describes the scope and approach of the current study, supported by citation.

claim: A human homologous β-cardiac myosin IHM model (PDB 5TBY) was modeled to the tarantula IHM quasi-atomic structure PDB 3JBH.
source: Modeling a human homologous β-cardiac myosin IHM model (PDB 5TBY, newly reported here) to the newest tarantula IHM quasi-atomic structure PDB 3JBH (Alamo et al., 2016)
evidence: This describes the structural modeling approach used in the study.

claim: Putative interaction sites were identified in the human β-cardiac myosin IHM model.
source: we first identified putative interaction sites
evidence: This describes a key step in the analysis.

claim: All variants categorized as pathogenic (PVs) and likely pathogenic (LPVs) in MYH7, MYL2, and MYL3 were examined.
source: then examined the locations of all variants categorized as pathogenic (PVs) and likely pathogenic (LPVs) in MYH7, MYL2, and MYL3.
evidence: This describes the variants analyzed in the study.

claim: HCM and DCM variants differentially impact myosin MD functions and specific IHM interactions.
source: We demonstrate that HCM and DCM variants differentially impact myosin MD functions and specific IHM interactions
evidence: This is a main finding of the study.

claim: The differential impact of variants informs the mechanisms for failed contractile power in DCM and the markedly compromised relaxation and energetics in HCM.
source: data that informs the mechanisms for failed contractile power in DCM and the markedly compromised relaxation and energetics in HCM (Ashrafian et al., 2003, 2011).
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by citations.

claim: A homologous human β-cardiac myosin IHM structure (PDB 5TBY) was modeled based on the tarantula striated muscle IHM quasi-atomic cryo-EM structure (PDB 3JBH).
source: We modeled a homologous human β-cardiac myosin IHM structure (Figure 2A and Video 1; deposited as entry PDB 5TBY) based on the tarantula striated muscle IHM quasi-atomic cryo-EM structure (PDB 3JBH, Alamo et al., 2016; Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes the structural modeling performed in the study, with reference to Figure 2A and Video 1.

claim: Although resolution of the IHM structure as derived by cryo-EM does not define specific atomic contacts or individual side chain densities, this model nonetheless identifies molecular interactions.
source: Although resolution of the IHM structure as derived by cryo-EM does not define specific atomic contacts or individual side chain densities, this model nonetheless identifies molecular interactions.
evidence: This acknowledges a limitation of the model while asserting its utility.

claim: The PDB 5TBY model fitted well to the 28 Å resolution 3D-reconstruction for the negatively stained human cardiac thick filament (EMD-2240).
source: The new model fitted well to the 28 Å resolution 3D-reconstruction for the negatively stained human cardiac thick filament (EMD-2240)(Al-Khayat et al., 2013) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This describes validation of the model by fitting to experimental data, with reference to Figure 2A.

claim: The predicted SAXS profile of PDB 5TBY is consistent with X-ray solution scattering of squid HMM in Ca2+-free (EGTA) conditions.
source: In addition, the predicted SAXS profile of PDB 5TBY is consistent with X-ray solution scattering of squid HMM in Ca2+-free (EGTA) conditions (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1) and the computed scattering profile for the model closely agrees with the measured scattering profile of squid heavy meromyosin (HMM) (Gillilan et al., 2013).
evidence: This describes additional validation of the model using SAXS data, with references to figures.

claim: The χ goodness of fit parameters for 3JBH and 5TBY are 1.5 and 1.85 respectively.
source: The χ goodness of fit parameters reported by the FoXS program are 1.5 for 3JBH and 1.85 for 5TBY respectively (Schneidman-Duhovny et al., 2013).
evidence: This provides quantitative measures of model fit to experimental data.

claim: The tarantula PDB 3JBH and the human PDB 5TBY models cannot be distinguished based on currently available SAXS data.
source: Relative deviation between the 5TBY and 3JBH calculated scattering profiles (dashed line) falls below the noise level of the experimental data (red line) consequently the two models cannot be distinguished.
evidence: This describes the similarity between the two models based on SAXS analysis.

claim: The PDB 5TBY model closely matches crystal structures of fragments for human β-cardiac S1 MD fragment (PDB 4DB1) and S2 (PDB 2FXM).
source: The PDB 5TBY model also closely matches crystal structures of fragments for human β-cardiac S1 MD fragment (PDB 4DB1) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A and Video 2) and S2 (PDB 2FXM)(Blankenfeldt et al., 2006) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B and Video 3).
evidence: This describes validation of the model by comparison to crystal structures, with references to figures and videos.

claim: The PDB 5TBY model includes important myosin loops that improve the analyses of IHM interactions, and that are absent from the only other IHM model used for cardiac muscle (PDB 3DTP).
source: Moreover, this model includes important myosin loops that improve the analyses of IHM interactions, and that are absent from the only other IHM model used for cardiac muscle (PDB 3DTP; Alamo et al., 2008).
evidence: This describes an advantage of the new model over prior models.

claim: In the PDB 5TBY model, the blocked and free myosin heads are in the pre-powerstroke state and bent at the 'pliant region'.
source: In the PDB 5TBY model, the blocked and free myosin heads are in the pre-powerstroke state (Xu et al., 2003; Zoghbi et al., 2004; Llinas et al., 2015) and bent at the 'pliant region' (Houdusse et al., 2000) (see Figure 2—figure supplement 2C and Video 4).
evidence: This describes structural features of the model, supported by citations and references to figures.

claim: The blocked head is in a pre-powerstroke state similar to the Mg·ADP-AlF4, PDB 1BR1.
source: The blocked head is in a pre-powerstroke state (Llinas et al., 2015) (similar to the Mg·ADP-AlF4, PDB 1BR1; [Liu et al., 2003; Alamo et al., 2008])
evidence: This describes the conformational state of the blocked head, supported by citations.

claim: The free head is in a pre-powerstroke state and shows a less angled lever arm than the blocked head.
source: while the free head, which is also in a pre-powerstroke state, shows a less angled lever arm than the blocked head (see Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This describes the conformational state of the free head, with reference to a figure.

claim: The homologous human β-cardiac myosin IHM model PDB 5TBY provides a robust option for analyses of cardiomyopathy variants on IHM interactions in the absence of a human β-cardiac IHM crystal atomic structure.
source: In the absence of a human β-cardiac IHM crystal atomic structure, the homologous human β-cardiac myosin IHM model PDB 5TBY (Figure 2A and Video 1) provides a robust option for analyses of cardiomyopathy variants on IHM interactions.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the utility of the model for the study.

claim: All sarcomere PVs and LPVs previously identified in 6112 HCM and 1315 DCM cases were analyzed.
source: All sarcomere PVs and LPVs previously identified in 6112 HCM and 1315 DCM cases (Walsh et al., 2017) were analyzed.
evidence: This describes the scope of variant analysis.

claim: Among HCM cases, 40 MYH7 PVs substituted 39 distinct aa at 33 positions and 95 LPVs led to 95 substitutions at 87 sites.
source: Among HCM cases, 40 MYH7 PVs substituted 39 distinct aa (two distinct variants encoded an identical substitution) at 33 positions and 95 LPVs led to 95 substitutions at 87 sites (Tables 1 and 2).
evidence: This provides quantitative data on HCM variants analyzed.

claim: Thirty-eight HCM PVs altered S1 and S2 residues, and two altered LMM residues.
source: Thirty-eight PVs altered S1 and S2 residues, and two altered LMM residues.
evidence: This describes the distribution of HCM PVs across myosin domains.

claim: Four HCM PVs occurred in ELC (n = 2) or RLC (n = 2).
source: Four further HCM PVs occurred in ELC (n = 2) or RLC (n = 2).
evidence: This describes HCM PVs in light chain genes.

claim: Among DCM cases, one MYH7 PV and 26 LPVs altered 26 distinct aa residues.
source: Among DCM cases, one MYH7 PV and 26 LPVs altered 26 distinct aa residues (Table 3).
evidence: This provides quantitative data on DCM variants analyzed.

claim: Similar proportions of HCM and DCM variants (26–29%) impact myosin residues with MD functions, albeit with distinctly different distributions.
source: We demonstrate that similar proportions of HCM and DCM variants (26–29%) impact myosin residues with MD functions, albeit with distinctly different distributions.
evidence: This is a key finding comparing HCM and DCM variants.

claim: DCM variants were enriched only in the nucleotide-binding site (p=0.00019) but were notably absent from the converter domain.
source: DCM variants were enriched only in the nucleotide-binding site (p=0.00019) but were notably absent from the converter domain, a region where residues also function in IHM interactions.
evidence: This describes the distribution of DCM variants with statistical significance.

claim: HCM variants are highly enriched in the converter domain (p=1.25e-8) and on the mesa (p=3.89e-12).
source: By contrast, HCM variants are highly enriched in the converter domain (p=1.25e-8) and on the mesa (p=3.89e-12)
evidence: This describes the distribution of HCM variants with statistical significance.

claim: HCM variants were 1.19-fold enriched in residues involved only in MD functions, 1.74-fold enriched in residues involved only in IHM interactions, and 4.17-fold enriched in residues that participate in both.
source: Indeed, HCM variants were 1.19-fold enriched in residues involved only in MD functions, 1.74-fold enriched in residues involved only in IHM interactions, and 4.17-fold enriched in residues that participate in both
evidence: This provides quantitative enrichment data for HCM variants.

claim: The enrichment pattern provides an account for why HCM PVs and LPVs, unlike DCM variants, have broad effects throughout the contraction and relaxation phases of the cardiac cycle.
source: providing an account for why HCM PVs and LPVs, unlike DCM variants, have broad effects throughout the contraction and relaxation phases of the cardiac cycle (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the enrichment data, with reference to Figure 1B.

claim: The location of HCM variants within functional MD residues of myosin, in vitro motility assays, and single molecule biophysical studies provide mechanisms for abnormal contractility.
source: While the location of HCM variants within functional MD residues of myosin, in vitro motility assays, and single molecule biophysical studies (Tyska et al., 2000; Spudich, 2014; Spudich et al., 2016) provide mechanisms for abnormal contractility
evidence: This summarizes prior evidence for contractility effects, supported by citations.

claim: Prior studies do not account for the prevalent and profound relaxation deficits that characterize HCM.
source: these do not account for the prevalent and profound relaxation deficits that characterize HCM.
evidence: This identifies a gap in prior understanding.

claim: Evidence that HCM variants in MYH7, MYL2, and MYL3 alter residues that support the dynamic properties of IHM provide mechanisms by which these disrupt cardiac relaxation and energetics.
source: By contrast, evidence that HCM variants in MYH7, MYL2, and MYL3 alter residues that support the dynamic properties of IHM provide mechanisms by which these disrupt cardiac relaxation and energetics (Figure 1A, Figure 3—figure supplement 5; see Material and methods).
evidence: This is a main conclusion of the study, with references to figures.

claim: HCM variants that impair IHM interactions would reduce SRX:DRX proportion, promote additional myosin-actin interactions, and consume more ATP, resulting in altered relaxation, energetics and force production.
source: HCM variants that impair IHM interactions would reduce SRX:DRX proportion, promote additional myosin-actin interactions, and consume more ATP, resulting in altered relaxation, energetics and force production.
evidence: This is a mechanistic conclusion drawn from the structural analysis.

claim: Previous studies of selected cardiomyopathy variants suggested that these might impact IHM formation.
source: Previous studies of selected cardiomyopathy variants, that employed early thick filament and IHM structures, suggested that these might impact IHM formation (Blankenfeldt et al., 2006; Alamo et al., 2008; Moore et al., 2012).
evidence: This summarizes prior limited studies, supported by citations.

claim: The current study advances prior conclusions by capitalizing on a novel human β-cardiac myosin IHM PDB 5TBY structure to consider if cardiomyopathy residues altered specific IHM interactions.
source: Our study advances these conclusions in several ways. Capitalizing on a novel human β-cardiac myosin IHM PDB 5TBY structure we considered if cardiomyopathy residues altered specific IHM interactions.
evidence: This describes an advance made by the current study.

claim: The study examined a comprehensive and unselected set of PVs and LPVs that were independently identified in a large cardiomyopathy cohort (7427 HCM and DCM patients) and compared these to variants in 33,370 ExAC controls.
source: Second, we studied a comprehensive and unselected set of PVs and LPVs that were independently identified in a large cardiomyopathy cohort (7427 HCM and DCM patients) and compared these to variants in 33,370 ExAC controls.
evidence: This describes the scope and rigor of the current study.

claim: Only HCM variants were significantly enriched in many IHM interacting residues, most notably in those that stabilize the IHM (p=5.37e-16 vs. expectation).
source: We found that only HCM variants were significantly enriched in many IHM interacting residues, most notably in those that stabilize the IHM (p=5.37e-16 vs. expectation).
evidence: This is a key statistical finding of the study.

claim: Most HCM variants resulted in a charge change, which are expected to adversely affect IHM interactions.
source: As most HCM variants resulted in a charge change (Tables 1 and 2), these are expected to adversely affect IHM interactions.
evidence: This is an inference about the functional consequences of charge changes.

claim: The data provide strong support that HCM variants perturb cardiac relaxation by disrupting IHM interactions.
source: Taken together, these data provide strong support that HCM variants perturb cardiac relaxation by disrupting IHM interactions.
evidence: This is a main conclusion of the study.

claim: A corollary to the conclusion is that the IHM interacting residues identified by the PDB 5TBY structure are physiologically valid.
source: A corollary to this conclusion is that the IHM interacting residues identified by the PDB 5TBY structure are physiologically valid.
evidence: This is an inference about the validity of the structural model.

claim: There are neither atomic nor near-atomic structures of the human cardiac IHM.
source: First, there are neither atomic nor near-atomic structures of the human cardiac IHM.
evidence: This acknowledges a limitation of the study.

claim: A near-atomic (0.6 nm) structure of the Lethocerus thick filament backbone has been reported, but the resolution for the IHM is comparable (2.0 nm) to the tarantula structure.
source: Although a near-atomic (0.6 nm) structure of the Lethocerus thick filament backbone has been reported (Hu et al., 2016), the resolution for the IHM is comparable (2.0 nm) to the tarantula structure employed here, perhaps because the intrinsic flexibility of swaying free heads limits higher resolution (Brito et al., 2011; Sulbarán et al., 2013).
evidence: This discusses limitations of available structures, supported by citations.

claim: Using homologous MYH7 sequences, the tarantula (PDB 3JBH) was converted into a human (PDB 5TBY) IHM model, which fits well into the human beta-cardiac 3D-reconstruction.
source: Second, using homologous MYH7 sequences, we converted the tarantula (PDB 3JBH) into a human (PDB 5TBY) IHM model, which fits well into the human beta-cardiac 3D-reconstruction (Figure 2a).
evidence: This describes the modeling approach and validation.

claim: The modeling capitalizes on the high evolutionary conservation between human MYH7 and tarantula striated myosin (60% amino acid identity), especially residues involved in IHM interactions.
source: While capitalizing on the high evolutionary conservation between human MYH7 and tarantula striated myosin (60% amino acid identity), especially residues involved in IHM interactions (Alamo et al., 2016)
evidence: This justifies the modeling approach based on sequence conservation, supported by citation.

claim: Future models are expected to refine the resolution of interactions identified in the PDB 5TBY model.
source: we expect that future models will refine the resolution of interactions identified in the PDB 5TBY model.
evidence: This is a speculation about future improvements.

claim: The tarantula striated muscle lacks MyBP-C and titin, molecules that may interact with IHMs to form helices in vertebrate thick filaments.
source: Third, the tarantula striated muscle lacks MyBP-C and titin, molecules that may interact with IHMs to form helices that protrude from vertebrate thick filaments and limit interactions between myosin heads and actin (Alamo et al., 2008; Jung et al., 2008; Luther et al., 2011).
evidence: This acknowledges a limitation of the tarantula model, supported by citations.

claim: The locations of several HCM variants hint that these may have additional functional consequences that impair interactions between consecutive IHMs.
source: The locations of several HCM variants hint that these may have additional functional consequences that impair interactions between consecutive IHMs.
evidence: This is a speculation about additional effects of HCM variants.

claim: While the data support the conclusion that the structural states defined by the IHM are responsible for the DRX and SRX functional states, these cannot be proven to be synonymous.
source: Fourth, while our data support the conclusion that the structural states defined by the IHM are responsible for the DRX and SRX functional states, these cannot be proven to be synonymous.
evidence: This acknowledges a limitation in proving the relationship between structural and functional states.

claim: High-resolution human cardiac thick filament structures are expected to extend insights to other HCM genes and variants.
source: We also expect that high-resolution human cardiac thick filament structures will extend these insights to other HCM genes and variants.
evidence: This is a speculation about future research directions.

claim: MyBP-C harbors many HCM variants that reduce protein levels and evoke functional consequences similar to MyBP-C phosphorylation.
source: MyBP-C harbors many HCM variants that reduce protein levels (Harris et al., 2011) and evoke functional consequences similar to MyBP-C phosphorylation: increase calcium sensitivity of active force and acceleration of rigor force and rigor stiffness development (Kunst et al., 2000).
evidence: This describes the effects of MyBP-C variants, supported by citations.

claim: The C1C2 fragment of MyBP-C is predicted to interact with the second of three negatively charged rings on the myosin S2 domain.
source: The C1C2 fragment of MyBP-C (Gruen and Gautel, 1999) is predicted to interact with the second of three negatively charged rings (Blankenfeldt et al., 2006) on the myosin S2 domain (Figure 2A and Figure 4, labeled as R1-3)
evidence: This describes a predicted interaction, supported by citations and references to figures.

claim: Ring 2 residues participate in stabilizing the IHM.
source: and Ring 2 residues participate in stabilizing the IHM.
evidence: This describes a functional role of Ring 2 residues.

claim: Charge inverting (+2) variants on Ring 2 (E924K and E930K) could disrupt MyBP-C binding and destabilize the IHM.
source: Charge inverting (+2) variants on Ring 2 (E924K and E930K in Table 1 and Figure 3—figure supplement 4 'a'; E927K and E935K, described in (Blankenfeldt et al., 2006) could disrupt MyBP-C binding (Lee et al., 2015), and destabilize the IHM
evidence: This is an inference about the effects of specific variants, supported by citations.

claim: HCM variants that deplete MyBP-C protein levels would destabilize the IHM.
source: as would HCM variants that deplete MyBP-C protein levels.
evidence: This is an inference about the effects of MyBP-C depletion.

claim: Destabilization of the IHM could account for the significant reduction of SRX that occurs in mice lacking MyBP-C.
source: Moreover, destabilization of the IHM could account for the significant reduction of SRX that occurs in mice lacking MyBP-C (McNamara et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an inference connecting IHM destabilization to experimental observations, supported by citation.

claim: Altered physiologic ratios of SRX and DRX populations is the mechanism by which HCM disrupts cardiac relaxation.
source: With the enrichment of MYH7 variants in IHM interacting residues reported here, we suggest that altered physiologic ratios of SRX and DRX populations is the mechanism by which HCM disrupts cardiac relaxation.
evidence: This is the main mechanistic conclusion of the study.

claim: HCM and DCM are dominant disorders and sarcomeres contain an admixture of normal and mutated myosin proteins.
source: HCM and DCM are dominant disorders and sarcomeres contain an admixture of normal and mutated myosin proteins.
evidence: This describes the genetic nature of these diseases.

claim: MYH7 DCM variants primarily impact functional MD residues (e.g. nucleotide binding and hydrolysis), which will depress contractility in proportion to the summed force produced by myosins with and without variants.
source: As MYH7 DCM variants primarily impact functional MD residues (e.g. nucleotide binding and hydrolysis), these will depress contractility in proportion to the summed force produced by myosins with and without variants (Schmitt et al., 2006; Spudich et al., 2016), with concurrent reduction in ATP consumption.
evidence: This describes the mechanism of DCM pathogenesis, supported by citations.

claim: The under-performance of sarcomeres containing DCM variants promotes compensatory ventricular dilation to maintain circulatory demands.
source: The resultant under-performance of sarcomeres containing DCM variants promotes compensatory ventricular dilation (Frank-Starling mechanism) to maintain circulatory demands (Figure 1C).
evidence: This describes the compensatory mechanism in DCM, with reference to Figure 1C.

claim: HCM variants impact both MD functions and IHM properties.
source: By contrast, (Schmitt et al., 2006; Spudich et al., 2016) HCM variants impact both MD functions and IHM properties.
evidence: This is a key finding distinguishing HCM from DCM variants.

claim: Any pair of myosins involved in asymmetric IHM interactions may contain zero, one, or two mutated residues with singular or dual consequences when located on the blocked or free head.
source: Any pair of myosins involved in asymmetric IHM interactions may contain zero, one, or two mutated residues with singular or dual consequences when located on the blocked or free head (Tables 1 and 2, Figure 3).
evidence: This describes the complexity of variant effects in the IHM context.

claim: The 135 HCM PVs and LPVs will alter 39 functional MD residues on each head and 73 IHM interacting residues, located on the blocked or free heads or S2 domain.
source: The 135 HCM PVs and LPVs described here will alter 39 functional MD residues on each head and 73 IHM interacting residues, located on the blocked or free heads or S2 domain (Supplementary file 3f).
evidence: This summarizes the scope of variant effects.

claim: 41 of 135 HCM variants altered only one IHM interaction, while 32 altered residues involved in at least two interactions simultaneously.
source: Notably, 41 of these 135 variants altered only one IHM interaction, while 32 altered residues involved in at least two interactions simultaneously, typically a different one for each head (Tables 1 and 2).
evidence: This describes the complexity of variant effects on IHM interactions.

claim: The effects of HCM variants on contractility and the multiple effects on IHM interactions confers a complexity that can explain dissimilar results obtained when myosin mutations are studied in different experimental contexts.
source: We suggest that the effects of HCM variants on contractility, their consequences on MD functions, and the multiple effects on IHM interactions, confers a complexity that can explain the dissimilar results obtained when myosin mutations are studied in the context of single myosin molecules that only assess MD functions and myofibril experiments that also interrogate the IHM (Moore et al., 2012).
evidence: This is an inference explaining discrepancies in prior experimental results, supported by citation.

claim: R453C can simultaneously affect IHM priming ('g' interaction) when located on the blocked head and stabilization ('d.1') when on the free head.
source: For example, R453C can simultaneously affect IHM priming ('g' interaction) when located on the blocked head (Figure 3—figure supplement 2) and stabilization ('d.1') when on the free head (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is an example of a variant with multiple effects, with references to figures.

claim: Biomechanical assays of myosin R453C show decreased actin-sliding velocity and ATPase, but increased force production.
source: Biomechanical assays of myosin R453C shows decreased actin-sliding velocity and ATPase, but increased force production (Sommese et al., 2013).
evidence: This describes experimental results for a specific variant, supported by citation.

claim: The dichotomous results for R453C may be explained by the IHM paradigm.
source: These dichotomous results may be explained by the IHM paradigm (Figures 1B and 3A).
evidence: This is an inference explaining experimental results using the IHM model, with references to figures.

claim: Located near the switch 2 with the nucleotide-binding pocket, R453C would impair S1 functions that are assayed by single molecule in vitro analyses.
source: Located near the switch 2 with the nucleotide-binding pocket, R453C would impair S1 functions that are assayed by single molecule in vitro analyses.
evidence: This is an inference about the effect of R453C on MD function.

claim: When located on the blocked head, the charge change of R453C (Δq = −2) would destabilize blocked myosin heads and increase the number of heads available for force potentiation.
source: When located on the blocked head ('g', Figure 3—figure supplement 2) the charge change of R453C (Δq = −2) would destabilize blocked myosin heads and increase the number of heads (the released blocked head and the associated partner free heads) that are available for force potentiation.
evidence: This is an inference about the effect of R453C on IHM stability, with reference to a figure.

claim: The increase in sarcomere force observed with many HCM variants likely reflects the combined effect on MD functions and IHM interactions that increase myosin populations in DRX and reduce those in SRX states.
source: As such, the increase in sarcomere force observed with many HCM variants likely reflects the combined effect on MD functions and IHM interactions that increase myosin populations in DRX and reduce those in SRX states.
evidence: This is an inference about the mechanism of increased force in HCM.

claim: HCM variants will impact cardiac physiology because of the relationship between the proportion of myosins in the DRX and SRX states and energy consumption.
source: HCM variants will further impact cardiac physiology because of the relationship between the proportion of myosins in the DRX and SRX states and energy consumption (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is an inference about the energetic consequences of HCM variants, with reference to Figure 1B.

claim: Swaying free myosin heads in the DRX state consume 5-fold greater ATP than in the SRX state.
source: Swaying free myosin heads in the DRX state consume 5-fold greater ATP than in the SRX state (Hooijman et al., 2011)
evidence: This describes the energetic difference between DRX and SRX states, supported by citation.

claim: Physiologic SRX:DRX levels during relaxation may reduce energy consumption and support life-long continuous activity.
source: and physiologic SRX:DRX levels during relaxation may reduce energy consumption and support life-long continuous activity.
evidence: This is an inference about the physiological role of SRX:DRX balance.

claim: By disrupting IHM interactions, HCM variants would reciprocally increase the proportion of myosins in the DRX state and decrease the proportion in the SRX state, resulting in increased ATP consumption and metabolic demands.
source: By disrupting IHM interactions, HCM variants would reciprocally increase the proportion of myosins in the DRX state and decreased the proportion in the SRX state – resulting in increased ATP consumption and metabolic demands, yielding energy deficiencies that characterize human HCM hearts (Ashrafian et al., 2003).
evidence: This is an inference about the mechanism of energy deficiency in HCM, supported by citation.

claim: These observations provide a plausible mechanistic explanation for why MYK-461, an ATPase inhibitor, improved the pathophysiology in HCM mouse models.
source: These observations also provide a plausible mechanistic explanation for why MYK-461, an ATPase inhibitor, improved the pathophysiology in HCM mouse models (Green et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an inference connecting the study's findings to therapeutic effects, supported by citation.

claim: The integrated interpretation of HCM and DCM variants on myosin MD functions and dynamic IHM interactions provides a fuller understanding of sarcomere biology in health and disease.
source: In summary, the integrated interpretation of HCM and DCM variants on myosin MD functions and dynamic IHM interactions provides a fuller understanding of sarcomere biology in health and disease.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the study's contribution.

claim: DCM variants evoke primary deficits in MD functions.
source: While DCM variants evoke primary deficits in MD functions (Figure 1C)
evidence: This is a conclusion about DCM pathogenesis, with reference to Figure 1C.

claim: HCM variants perturb both MD functions and IHM interactions.
source: HCM variants perturb both MD functions and IHM interactions (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a conclusion about HCM pathogenesis, with reference to Figure 1B.

claim: By disrupting IHM priming, anchoring, stability, and scaffolding interactions, HCM variants decrease populations of docked myosin heads (SRX) and increase swaying heads (DRX) that are available for force production, thereby promoting hypercontractility.
source: By disrupting IHM priming, anchoring, stability, and scaffolding interactions, HCM variants decrease populations of docked myosin heads (SRX) and increase swaying heads (DRX) that are available for force production, thereby promoting hypercontractility.
evidence: This is a mechanistic conclusion about HCM pathogenesis.

claim: The reduction of myosin populations in SRX would perturb diastolic relaxation and increase ATP consumption, causing energy deficiencies in HCM hearts.
source: The reduction of myosin populations in SRX would perturb diastolic relaxation and increase ATP consumption, causing energy deficiencies in HCM hearts (Ashrafian et al., 2003).
evidence: This is a mechanistic conclusion about HCM pathophysiology, supported by citation.

claim: These are primary biophysical deficits produced directly by HCM variants that are unrelated to secondary compensatory changes observed in other heart diseases.
source: Notably, these are primary biophysical deficits produced directly by HCM variants that are unrelated to secondary compensatory changes observed in other heart diseases.
evidence: This distinguishes primary from secondary effects in HCM.

claim: Clinical observations support the conclusion that hyperdynamic contraction, diastolic dysfunction, and energy deficiency precede hypertrophic remodeling in young HCM variant mutation carriers.
source: Clinical observations support this conclusion: hyperdynamic contraction, diastolic dysfunction (Ho et al., 2002), and energy deficiency (Jung et al., 1998; Crilley et al., 2003) precedes hypertrophic remodeling in young HCM variant mutation carriers.
evidence: This cites clinical evidence supporting the mechanistic conclusions, with citations.

claim: The identification of sarcomere protein residues involved in relaxation provide new opportunities to target the IHM to improve HCM pathophysiology and other heart diseases with diastolic dysfunction.
source: We conclude that the identification of sarcomere protein residues involved in relaxation provide new opportunities to target the IHM to improve HCM pathophysiology and other heart diseases with diastolic dysfunction.
evidence: This is a conclusion about therapeutic implications.

claim: Extension of these analyses to skeletal myopathies is anticipated to provide further insights into critical roles of the highly conserved IHM in the relaxation of striated muscles.
source: By extension of these analyses to skeletal myopathies we anticipate further insights into critical roles of the highly conserved IHM in the relaxation of striated muscles.
evidence: This is a speculation about future research directions.
